messages:
Lina (Product): FYI from user tests: clicking the little 'Docs' link next to settings opens the docs root. Users expected the exact control doc.

Jules (Design): I noticed the same. The floating side-help links are generic. It feels like we lose context. Mobile is worse because the fragment target sits under the sticky header.

Kendrick (Docs): Our static generator creates anchors from headings which change when copy iterates. That's the source of stale fragments.

Jules (Design): Could we add explicit IDs on docs headings? e.g. `### Model routing {#model-routing}` so console links to `/docs/console/routing#model-routing`.

Kendrick (Docs): Yes. Proposal: authors add explicit kebab-case IDs for any heading we expect to deep-link. I'll draft a short author guideline.

Sam (QA): Also want a test case: verify 3 random deep links land at the visible heading (desktop + mobile) and that the heading gets keyboard focus. We keep missing that in regression.

Lina (Product): Agreed. Also let's settle on naming: UI shows "Help" in some places, "Docs" in others, and the site title says "Documentation". It's confusing. I propose the in-app label be "Docs" (short).

Kendrick (Docs): Sounds good. I'll update the lexicon and the docs site frontmatter to show "Redwood Console docs" as the canonical page title.

Jules (Design): UX detail: when jumping to a fragment, apply a 64px offset to account for the fixed header, then `element.focus()` with `tabindex="-1"`. Add a soft highlight animation so users can see where they landed.

Sam (QA): Accessibility: ensure the focus event is announced by screen readers. Also ensure any toast fallback is announced (`role="status"`).

Kendrick (Docs): For fallbacks, if an anchor is missing we should redirect to the page root and show a toast: "Section moved — opening docs home" with a search link. I'll add a redirect alias table in the docs repo for renamed anchors.

Jules (Design): Small enhancement: the side-help could fetch a 1-line preview for the anchor and show it in a tooltip so users know what they're opening. DevEx could provide an API for that.

Lina (Product): Good idea. Owners: Kendrick = anchor IDs + redirect table, Jules = UI offset + preview UX, Sam = QA deep-link tests, Lina = lexicon update + KB note.

AssistBot: Actions recorded: docs-add-stable-ids (Kendrick), ui-anchor-offset-and-preview (Jules), qa-deep-link-regression (Sam), lexicon-rename-docs (Lina).

Kendrick (Docs): I'll add IDs to the top 10 most-linked pages first and include examples of canonical links in the PR description (format: `https://docs.redwood.inference/console/<page>#<kebab-anchor>`).

Jules (Design): I'll prototype offset+preview and share a short video. If API isn't ready, I'll mock the preview content.

Sam (QA): I'll add the checklist and include a keyboard-only flow: open link, landing focus, press tab to continue.

Lina (Product): Thanks team. Ping when the QA ticket and the docs PR are up and we'll schedule the console patch.
